newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Thursday on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,125 yuan ($376) per tonne, losing 27 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,145 and hit a low of 3,122.
March fell 63 to 3,086, May 21 to 3,200, July 39 to 3,291, September rose 20 to 3,388 and November 18 to 3,398.
Combined volume fell to 17,100 tonnes from 21,900.
Traders said the key contracts stayed below the key 3,200-yuan support level in the past few days, which discouraged long position holders seriously.
"Many investors expected soybeans to fall further after breaching the 3,200-yuan level, resulting in panic selling today," one trader said.
"Soybeans are likely to continue to fall in the next few days due to poor fundamentals, but not sharply," he added.
Analysts said domestic bumper harvests and more imports put pressure on soybeans at high levels.
